column1: # The ESCAPE HATCH, and nothing else. Empty is the normal state.
# Failures explained by a SUBSTITUTION are not listed here and must not be: they are DERIVED. A
# test whose failure stack reaches a type in this port's `Substitutions.dropTypes` fails because
# the port deliberately does not have that type, and `PortRun` writes those FQNs to
# `run-latest/dropped-types.tsv` on every run for `balticporter.tir.Correlate` to read. The four
# `com.badlogic.gdx.utils.JsonTest` failures this file used to list by hand are classified that
# way now, and the list follows the manifest without anyone editing it.
# What belongs here is a failure NO DROP EXPLAINS and that is still a decision rather than a
# regression — an upstream test asserting a JVM-only behaviour, a test whose fixture the port
# cannot supply. Each such line is a CLAIM someone has to defend, which is why it is kept apart
# from the derived set: `test-failures.tsv` records `expected#declared` vs `expected#derived`, and
# a declared entry whose test starts PASSING is reported so it can be deleted. A hand-maintained
# list of expected failures is exactly the thing that rots into "we always ignore those four" and
# then hides a fifth.
# `test` may be `*` to declare a whole suite.
# A row may also carry `frame=<ported class>` as a trailing TAB-separated field — the `unit` the
# correlator anchors the failure at, copied from `run-latest/test-failures.tsv`. While it holds the
# row classifies as before; where it stops holding the failure counts UNEXPECTED and the entry is
# reported as a reason that no longer holds. It is OPTIONAL because these files predate it, and a
# row without one keeps exactly the old behaviour — but a claim keyed on the test's NAME alone
# absorbs a NEW failure with a DIFFERENT cause in the same test, silently, which is the same rot
# one column over. New rows should carry it.
#suite
